To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a new on-line parameter identification theory for infinite-dimensional dynamical linear systems and for nonlinear systems, and that we have demonstrated the effectiveness of this theory in a series of numerical experiments.

(1) an on-line or adaptive algorithm for estimating the parameters in infinite-dimensional linear and nonlinear systems is defined, and convergence is established; (2) a theory of finite-dimensional approximations is developed and convergence results established; and (3) numerical results for examples involving both linear and nonlinear systems with constant and functional parameters are presented.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the on-line estimation of parameters in abstract infinite-dimensional linear and nonlinear systems.
on-line or adaptive parameter identification in linear or nonlinear infinite-dimensional dynamically evolving systems.

the development and study of a class of adaptive observers and parameter estimators for a broad class of linear and nonlinear infinite dimensional dynamical systems, including systems described by partial differential equations.

the results obtained in the present paper are a first step in the development of on-line parameter estimation theory for infinite-dimensional systems.
the theory of on-line parameter estimation in infinite-dimensional systems is well established, with a number of examples demonstrating that the theory is applicable to practical problems.
the results obtained for infinite-dimensional dynamical system estimation are very similar to those obtained in finite-dimensional system estimation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed the mathematical theory and the numerical algorithms for a new class of parameter estimation problems in infinite-dimensional systems.
the on-line parameter identification of infinite-dimensional linear and nonlinear dynamical systems is possible and can be accomplished by using an infinite-dimensional state estimator.
we have shown how to estimate the parameters in a class of infinite-dimensional linear and nonlinear dynamical systems on-line.
The main takeaway from our work is that
on-line parameter estimation is feasible for infinite-dimensional dynamical processes and that the theory is not fundamentally different from that for finite-dimensional systems.

, in general, the estimation of parameters in infinite-dimensional systems is a much harder problem than the estimation of parameters for finite-dimensional systems, and the convergence rates of the parameter estimates are much slower.
the parameter estimation problem can be formulated as an infinite-dimensional linear or nonlinear control problem, which can be solved by a number of existing numerical methods.
